title: Which teams have been been relegated from the Bundesliga in 2022-23? | DraftKings Network
content: With the 2022-23 Bundesliga season drawing to a close this weekend, Matchday 34 features a tightly contested four-way battle to beat the drop and avoid relegation from Germany’s top flight. Hertha Berlin’s relegation was confirmed back on Matchday 33, as they conceded a disappointing equalizer in the last minute to draw 1-1 with Bochum. Schalke currently sit in 17th place with 31 points and with a 2-2 draw with Eintracht Frankfurt back on Matchday 33, it means they at least need one point on the final day of the season to avoid automatic relegation and potentially a relegation play-off altogether. Bochum sit in 16th place with 32 points and if the season were to end today, they would head into a relegation play-off to decide the club’s future in the Bundesliga for next season. A win against Bayer Leverkusen on the final day of the season will surely be enough to avoid automatic relegation, and potentially a play-off matchup as well.

title: Relegation Play-Offs | DFL Deutsche Fußball Liga
content: Home » Glossary » Relegation Play-Offs. # Relegation Play-Offs. At the end of each season, the bottom two clubs in the Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 are relegated to Bundesliga 2 and the 3. A two-legged relegation play-off is played between the club that finished third-last in the Bundesliga and the club that finished third in Bundesliga 2, and similarly between the club that finished third-last in Bundesliga 2 and the club that finished third in the 3. Liga, to determine whether the club from the higher division retains its status or whether the club from the lower division is promoted in its place. The matches are played using the knock-out format used in the European club competitions (“European Cup system”). The clubs play each other at home and away. Home advantage in the second leg is given to the club that had fewer match-free days prior to the first leg based on the fixture list for the past season.

title: Four games left: Which Bundesliga club has the highest risk of relegation?
content: Seven teams still have a risk of Bundesliga relegation: St. Pauli, VfL Wolfsburg, Heidenheim, 1. FC Köln, Hamburg, Werder Bremen and Borussia Mönchengladbach. A loss against St. Pauli sees Heidenheim confirmed down as the first Bundesliga relegated side this season. Due to personnel, they may feel like they have the upper hand in the relegation battle but they still play some tough fixtures like against Bayern Munich, Freiburg and at home to fellow relegation-battler Borussia Mönchengladbach. With a view to the final matchday, a lot may rest on their away tie against 16th St. Pauli with this match at the moment promising to be a real scrap for Bundesliga survival. With a 1-1 draw against Köln, it is clear to see that this result favoured the away side in their bid for survival in the Bundesliga. With 26 goals this season, St. Pauli are the Bundesliga's lowest scoring side and this showed against Köln as they left plenty of chances missing to win the game against score more.

title: German Football Promotions & Relegations, 2025-26 | Groundhopper Guides
content: ## **Here are the German Football Promotions, Relegations & European Places for the 2025-26 season.**. After every season, as it is all over Europe, German football clubs go up, go down, and get into Europe. Meanwhile, here is a post all about promotion and relegation in the top European football leagues. ### **League Structure in German Football**. At the top is the Bundesliga, including all the famous clubs like Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund and the rest. Connecting all of this, as in England, is a system of promotion and relegation. At the top of the Bundesliga, as in the Premier League, the top four clubs qualify for the next season’s Champions League. The winner of the domestic cup competition, the DFB-Pokal, also goes to the Europa League — and if that team also qualifies for Champions League or Europa League elsewhere, their spot in Europa goes to the next-highest finisher in the table who didn’t otherwise qualify for Europe.
